answer: Plant a share of tasks whose correct answer is already known, then watch who grades them wrong. A juror who waves a known-bad answer through loses that epoch's credit, and every submission carries a fresh nonce so a replayed spiral of old text is rejected at intake. Because payouts are capped per identity per epoch, volume buys nothing, and the ember of a fake grading ring dies on its first honeypot before the ripple reaches the honest pool.
